question: How often does a two-sample KS test on detector scores flag a batch that contains images from a new site, and how often does it flag a batch with none?

detectors.primary: mahalanobis (PCA size by method D; the shipped detector)

models: the three v2 centralized seeds (v2-final-seed0, -seed1, -seed2), each with its own detector fit; results per seed, then mean and range
reference: validation scores (v2 validation, 3,210 images) from each model's detector
reference_provenance: validation scores were not saved by the drift-table run, so a CPU job refits each detector on training images only and scores validation; it must reproduce the drift run's method-D PCA size and Gram layer normalizer for that model, or it stops. No test or shift image is touched.

pools.in_distribution: the drift run's saved scores for the clients' test split (3,262 images)

batch_construction: round(share x size) images drawn from the new site's pool and the rest from the in-distribution pool, each without replacement within a batch
test: two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov (scipy.stats.ks_2samp, two-sided), batch vs reference

reported.detection_rate: share of batches with p < 0.01, per site, batch size and share (shares above 0%)
reported.false_alarm_rate: share of 0% batches (in-distribution test only) with p < 0.01, per batch size

caveat: the in-distribution pool is the clients' test split and the reference is validation; both are in-distribution, so the 0% false-alarm rate also measures any validation-to-test difference

rebuild_tolerance.method_d_pca_size: must equal the drift run's, or differ by at most 1 component; the drift run's own size is the one used to score validation
rebuild_tolerance.gram_normalizer: every layer's value within 0.1% relative difference of the drift run's
rebuild_tolerance.on_failure: stop and report; the tolerance is not loosened

false_alarm_rule: if 0% batches are flagged more than 2% of the time for any model and detector (at any batch size), that is reported as a finding: the validation baseline does not match in-distribution test. The baseline is not switched afterwards.
gram_normalizer_note: Gram's per-layer normalizer was fitted on these same validation images in the drift run (mean validation deviation per layer), so Gram's validation reference is not independent of its own normalization; this is stated with the results.
amended: 2026-10-04, before the reference job ran: rebuild tolerance and false-alarm rule added

amendment_2.reason: the reference job (run 828284284699299) stopped on the rebuild tolerance: v2-final-seed0's Gram normalizer differed from the GPU fit by up to 11.8% (tolerance 0.1%); its method-D PCA size matched exactly (541)
amendment_2.change: Gram is dropped from batch-level drift; only the shipped Mahalanobis detector (method D) is run

numerical_check.what: per centralized model, Mahalanobis scores recomputed on CPU (detector refit on CPU training features at the drift run's PCA size) for 300 benchmark evaluation images, 150 PathMNIST and 150 CIFAR-10, chosen by a seeded draw (seed 0) of positions in the drift run's saved arrays, compared with the drift run's saved GPU scores for the same images
numerical_check.scores_only: no AUROC or any other metric is computed from these images; it is a numerical comparison of scores
numerical_check.pass: Spearman rank correlation >= 0.999 and at least 99% of images within 1% relative difference

amendment_2.record: each model's check record (PCA sizes, normalizer not applicable, numerical check) is saved as soon as it is computed; finished models are skipped on a rerun
amendment_2.phase3_relevance: this tests recomputing the detector on CPU against the GPU fit; Phase 3 plans to fit on GPU and serve on CPU, where the GPU-fitted detector would be applied to CPU features

status.phase2: not run: the CPU reference failed the amendment-2 score check for v2-final-seed0 (run 186825054715071)
status.moved_to: Phase 3 (PLAN.md), same spec, with baseline and batches scored on the same CPU setup
added_rules: CPU re-scoring of test and new-site images does not reopen the detector choice; Mahalanobis stays shipped
any AUROC from CPU scores is reported only as a reproducibility check against the Phase 2 GPU table, never as a replacement
